question.problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$  

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x\cdot {\text{proj}}_{S}x}{‖x‖‖{\text{proj}}_{S}x‖} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 2+0\cdot (-2)+0\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{16}\sqrt{8}} \\  & =\frac{8}{4\cdot 2\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})=\frac{\pi }{4},
$$

which is already an acute angle.
